messages:
Lina: Hey team — customer Acme (Jane) is seeing 401s (invalid_api_key) only for some requests. They say it worked earlier and then started failing after they flipped an edge config ~2h ago.

Jane - AcmeClient: throwing 401s from production. curl from my laptop to the same endpoint works, but our app requests from Fastly return 401 with body: {"error":"invalid_api_key"}. No key rotation on our side.

Lina: can you paste request headers from the failing request?

Jane - AcmeClient: here's what our edge logs show for Authorization header (redacted):
Authorization: Bearer Bearer abc123def456gh==

Jane - AcmeClient: the app uses an axios interceptor to add the token, and our edge was also configured to forward/append auth headers for legacy reasons. Not sure which added the extra 'Bearer'.

Devon - Eng: interesting — that double-Bearer would produce an auth token starting with the literal 'Bearer '. Our auth parsing currently strips the first /^Bearer\s+/, so 'Bearer Bearer XYZ' -> token = 'Bearer XYZ' (i.e., still has leading 'Bearer '). That will obviously not match any stored key.

Devon - Eng: quick repro I ran locally: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer Bearer abc123def456gh==" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
returns 401 with body: {"error":"invalid_api_key"}

Devon - Eng: server log line for the failing request: 
```
ts=2026-03-15T12:04:23Z level=warn auth=failed api_key_value='Bearer abc123def456gh==' reason=not_found
```
Note how api_key_value contains a leading 'Bearer ' — that's from our parser only removing a single prefix.

Matt - Eng Runtime: that also explains intermittent nature — some requests (from laptop/curl) only had single Bearer and worked. Requests going through their edge had both and failed.

Lina: suggested mitigations? Immediate customer-facing option?

Devon - Eng: short term: ask customer to stop having edge add Authorization when app already sets it. Long term: we should harden the server to normalize the header. I'll prepare a small auth-service patch that repeatedly strips leading 'Bearer ' until it's gone, and add a metric to detect when token still contains non-hex junk. Will also add a FAQ entry for "double Bearer" mistakes.

Devon - Eng: patch ready, running canary now. Key changes:
- canonicalize token: while token.startsWith('Bearer ') token = token.slice(7).trim()
- add log that redacts token but indicates original prefix count

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for service=auth-service commit=7f3c9a2 (5% traffic)

Jane - AcmeClient: FYI we've updated our edge to stop appending Authorization header. Will monitor.

Lina: once canary is green we can promote. Also adding triage note: common copy/paste issues aside, watch for double header injection from proxy + client. Add to KB.

deploy-bot: canary success — promoted to prod in 12m (rollout id=canary-7f3c9a2).

Jane - AcmeClient: confirmed — after the change and your canary we now see 200s from the previously failing path. Thanks! :tada:

Lina: closing loop with customer. Internal action items: update auth parser, add diagnostic log that shows when token starts with 'Bearer ' more than once, and document troubleshooting steps (how to grep edge logs for 'Authorization' header and repro curl).

Devon - Eng: repro checklist for support KB:
1) Ask customer to paste raw Authorization header from failing request.
2) Try curl with header exactly as captured to reproduce.
3) Check server auth logs — look for api_key_value starting with 'Bearer '.
4) If double-Bearer found, advise edge/dev to stop duplicating header or await our normalization patch.

Lina: tagging internal docs task. Closing thread after follow-up doc created.

-- end of thread --
